post.caption: The oldest known geological map shows gold. It was drawn in Egypt around 1150 BC, under Ramesses IV, and it shows Wadi Hammamat, between the Nile and the Red Sea. The mapped stretch is about 9 miles long. It marks gold deposits and four small houses for the workers, and pink hills mark granite and gold-bearing quartz. A caption says the gold mountains are colored red. It was prepared for an expedition to quarry stone for royal statues, and south sits at the top of the map. It is kept in the Museo Egizio in Turin, Italy. The next known geological map came nearly 3,000 years later.
